verb-quiz-1.title: Weekly Quiz 1: Foundations: Learn How to Learn

questions.prompt: be → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of be: is.

questions.prompt: be → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of be: being.

questions.prompt: have → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of have: having.

questions.prompt: have → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of have: had.

questions.prompt: She ___ ready to study. (be)
questions.explanation: She is ready to study. (be)

questions.prompt: He ___ a reference sheet. (have)
questions.explanation: He has a reference sheet. (have)

questions.prompt: Which word means “to give your attention to one thing”?
questions.explanation: focus: to give your attention to one thing. Focus on one sentence at a time.

questions.prompt: You learned a rule. Now _____ it by using it in a new sentence.
questions.explanation: apply: to use what you learned. Apply the rule by writing a new sentence about yourself.

questions.prompt: In “The helpful teacher has a book,” which word describes the teacher?
questions.explanation: Helpful is an adjective. It describes the noun teacher.

questions.prompt: Fix one word: “She have a notebook.” Write the complete sentence.
questions.explanation: With she, the present form of have is has.

verb-quiz-2.title: Weekly Quiz 2: Digital Habits + Community Routines

questions.prompt: do → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of do: doing.

questions.prompt: do → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of do: did.

questions.prompt: make → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of make: made.

questions.prompt: make → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of make: made.

questions.prompt: What do you ___ after class? (do)
questions.explanation: What do you do after class? (do)

questions.prompt: She ___ a study plan every Sunday. (make)
questions.explanation: She makes a study plan every Sunday. (make)

questions.prompt: Click the button to _____ your homework before the deadline.
questions.explanation: submit: to send your work or information officially. Submit your answers before the timer runs out.

questions.prompt: Which word means “to open or enter a file, website, or building”?
questions.explanation: access: to open or enter a file, website, or building. You can access your lessons from any device.

questions.prompt: You want to know the location of the computer lab. Which question do you ask?
questions.explanation: Where asks about a place or location.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "___ is the English class? On Monday and Wednesday evenings." (Which question word asks about time?)
questions.explanation: When asks about a time. Monday and Wednesday evenings are times.

verb-quiz-3.title: Weekly Quiz 3: Getting Around: Directions + Digital Safety

questions.prompt: go → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of go: went.

questions.prompt: go → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of go: gone.

questions.prompt: come → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of come: come.

questions.prompt: come → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of come: comes.

questions.prompt: Yesterday, I ___ to the library. (go)
questions.explanation: Yesterday, I went to the library. (go)

questions.prompt: Please ___ to the front desk. (come)
questions.explanation: Please come to the front desk. (come)

questions.prompt: Which word means “to go in the same direction; to use directions step by step”?
questions.explanation: follow: to go in the same direction; to use directions step by step. Follow the signs to the emergency exit.

questions.prompt: _____ the street only when the walk signal is green.
questions.explanation: cross: to go from one side to the other. Cross the street at the crosswalk when the light is green.

questions.prompt: "She don't work on Sundays." What is wrong with this sentence?
options: Should be 'doesn't' because 'she' is third person singular.
Should be 'didn't' because it happened in the past.
answers: Should be 'doesn't' because 'she' is third person singular.
questions.explanation: With he/she/it in present simple negatives, use doesn't, not don't.

questions.prompt: Rosa describes her morning commute. Put the words in order. Words: She / usually / takes / the / bus / to / work
answers: She usually takes the bus to work
questions.explanation: Usually goes before the main verb: She usually takes.

verb-quiz-4.title: Weekly Quiz 4: Phone English + Family Connection

questions.prompt: tell → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of tell: told.

questions.prompt: tell → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of tell: tells.

questions.prompt: say → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of say: says.

questions.prompt: say → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of say: saying.

questions.prompt: Can you ___ me your phone number? (tell)
questions.explanation: Can you tell me your phone number? (tell)

questions.prompt: You should ___ your name clearly. (say)
questions.explanation: You should say your name clearly. (say)

questions.prompt: _____ the school office if your child will be absent.
questions.explanation: contact: to reach someone by phone, email, or message. Contact the school if your child will be absent.

questions.prompt: Which word means “to answer or react to a message or question”?
questions.explanation: respond: to answer or react to a message or question. Please respond to the email within 24 hours.

questions.prompt: "You don't have to use a special browser for online banking." What does this mean?
options: Using a special browser is forbidden.
Using a special browser is required.
Using a special browser is optional.
answers: Using a special browser is optional.
questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' means it is not required. It is different from 'must not,' which means it is forbidden.

questions.prompt: Claudette is setting up her phone at the library. Which sentence is correct?
options: She can uses the library wifi for free.
She can use the library wifi for free.
She can to use the library wifi for free.
answers: She can use the library wifi for free.
questions.explanation: Modal verbs (can, should, must) are always followed by the base verb with no changes.

questions.prompt: take → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of take: takes.

questions.prompt: take → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of take: taking.

questions.prompt: bring → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of bring: bringing.

questions.prompt: bring → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of bring: brought.

questions.prompt: Have you ever ___ food to a neighbor? (take)
questions.explanation: Have you ever taken food to a neighbor? (take)

questions.prompt: We have ___ extra bags for the volunteers. (bring)
questions.explanation: We have brought extra bags for the volunteers. (bring)

questions.prompt: Which word means “to help or encourage someone or a cause”?
questions.explanation: support: to help or encourage someone or a cause. Our community supports local families in need.

questions.prompt: Everyone can _____ time or money to help the community garden.
questions.explanation: contribute: to give time, money, or effort to help something. Everyone can contribute in a small way to make things better.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Have you ever ___ to a city council meeting?" (V3 of 'be')
questions.explanation: After 'have you ever', always use V3. The V3 of 'be' is 'been'.

questions.prompt: "Have you ever called 311?" Omar says no. What is the best reply?
questions.explanation: Short answer for Have you ever uses haven't (not didn't or don't).

questions.prompt: meet → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of meet: meeting.

questions.prompt: meet → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of meet: met.

questions.prompt: speak → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of speak: spoke.

questions.prompt: speak → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of speak: spoken.

questions.prompt: I enjoy ___ new neighbors. (meet)
questions.explanation: I enjoy meeting new neighbors. (meet)

questions.prompt: She is good at ___ in public. (speak)
questions.explanation: She is good at speaking in public. (speak)

questions.prompt: Most neighbors _____ with the plan to fix the streetlights.
questions.explanation: agree: to have the same opinion or say yes to something. Most people at the meeting agreed with the new plan.

questions.prompt: Which word means “to pay attention to what someone is saying”?
questions.explanation: listen: to pay attention to what someone is saying. Good leaders listen to the concerns of their community.

questions.prompt: Diego talks about his skills at the restaurant. Put the words in order. Words: I / am / good / at / cooking / fast
answers: I am good at cooking fast
questions.explanation: Good at + -ing. The verb after 'at' must end in -ing.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Don't sign without read the contract.
Don't sign without reading the contract.
Don't sign without to read the contract.
answers: Don't sign without reading the contract.
questions.explanation: 'Without' is a preposition. The verb after it must be -ing: without reading.

verb-quiz-7.title: Weekly Quiz 7: Our Voice, Our Vote

questions.prompt: write → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of write: wrote.

questions.prompt: write → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of write: written.

questions.prompt: send → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of send: sent.

questions.prompt: send → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of send: sends.

questions.prompt: Let’s ___ a letter to the council. (write)
questions.explanation: Let’s write a letter to the council. (write)

questions.prompt: Why don’t we ___ an email? (send)
questions.explanation: Why don’t we send an email? (send)

questions.prompt: Which word means “to officially choose a person or option in an election”?
questions.explanation: vote: to officially choose a person or option in an election. Register and vote in your local elections.

questions.prompt: In November, voters will _____ a new mayor.
questions.explanation: elect: to choose a person for a position by voting. Citizens elect leaders to represent them in government.

questions.prompt: Gloria wants the whole group to act together. Which sentence fits?
options: Let's meet in the lobby at six.
Let's to meet in the lobby at six.
Let's meeting in the lobby at six.
answers: Let's meet in the lobby at six.
questions.explanation: 'Let's' is always followed by the base verb with no changes.

questions.prompt: Kevin tells Marta that saving the repair receipts is the right and necessary step. Which fits?
options: You could save the repair receipts.
You should save the repair receipts.
answers: You should save the repair receipts.
questions.explanation: 'You should' gives stronger advice. 'You could' is a softer option, and 'Let's' suggests doing it together.

verb-quiz-8.title: Weekly Quiz 8: Fall Review + Class Party

questions.prompt: Which word means “to meet someone new and tell them your name”?
questions.explanation: Introduce: She introduced herself on the first day of class.

questions.prompt: Which word means “to pay close attention to one thing”?
questions.explanation: Focus: Focus on one section at a time when you study.

questions.prompt: Which word means “to leave a place to start a trip”?
questions.explanation: Depart: The bus departs at 7:15 every morning.

questions.prompt: Which word means “to offer to do something without being paid”?
questions.explanation: Volunteer: She volunteers at the food bank every Saturday.

questions.prompt: Which word means “to plan how much money to spend”?
questions.explanation: Budget: Budget your money so you can pay all your bills.

verb-quiz-9.title: Weekly Quiz 9: How Long + For and Since

questions.prompt: cost → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of cost: costs.

questions.prompt: cost → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of cost: costing.

questions.prompt: spend → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of spend: spending.

questions.prompt: spend → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of spend: spent.

questions.prompt: The smaller package ___ less than the large one. (cost)
questions.explanation: The smaller package costs less than the large one. (cost)

questions.prompt: Last week, we ___ less on groceries. (spend)
questions.explanation: Last week, we spent less on groceries. (spend)

questions.prompt: Which word means “to use money to pay for things”?
questions.explanation: spend: to use money to pay for things. Don't spend more than you earn.

questions.prompt: _____ the total cost, including tax, before you pay.
questions.explanation: calculate: to use math to find an answer. Calculate the total cost before you decide to buy.

questions.prompt: Beatriz's last day at the restaurant was Tuesday of last week. She does not work there anymore. Which sentence is correct?
options: Beatriz has left the restaurant since last Tuesday.
Beatriz has worked at the restaurant for last Tuesday.
Beatriz left the restaurant last Tuesday.
answers: Beatriz left the restaurant last Tuesday.
questions.explanation: A finished action with a specific past time (last Tuesday) needs past simple, not present perfect.

questions.prompt: Rosa has had her phone plan since 2021. She wants to say the same thing using 'for'. It is now 2024. What does she say?
options: I have had this plan for since three years.
I have had this plan for three years.
I have had this plan for 2021.
answers: I have had this plan for three years.
questions.explanation: 'For' takes a length of time, not a starting year. 2024 minus 2021 = three years.

verb-quiz-10.title: Weekly Quiz 10: More, Less, the Most: Comparatives + Superlatives

questions.prompt: buy → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of buy: buying.

questions.prompt: buy → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of buy: bought.

questions.prompt: sell → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of sell: sold.

questions.prompt: sell → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of sell: sold.

questions.prompt: Yesterday, I ___ the cheaper phone. (buy)
questions.explanation: Yesterday, I bought the cheaper phone. (buy)

questions.prompt: This shop ___ the most affordable furniture. (sell)
questions.explanation: This shop sells the most affordable furniture. (sell)

questions.prompt: This shirt is too small. I want to _____ it for a larger size.
questions.explanation: exchange: to return one item and get a different one. I want to exchange this shirt for a larger size.

questions.prompt: Which word means “to get your money back after returning something”?
questions.explanation: refund: to get your money back after returning something. The store gave me a full refund for the broken item.

questions.prompt: Kevin compares three ways to get to work. Which sentence is correct?
options: The Blue Line is the most fastest.
The Blue Line is the fastest.
answers: The Blue Line is the fastest.
questions.explanation: Superlatives need 'the' before them. Never add 'most' to an -est form.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "Plan B is ___ expensive than Plan A." (Long adjective comparative: don't add -er.)
questions.explanation: Long adjectives use 'more' for comparatives. Never add -er to a long adjective like 'expensive'.

verb-quiz-11.title: Weekly Quiz 11: How Much / How Many: Countable + Uncountable

questions.prompt: eat → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of eat: ate.

questions.prompt: eat → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of eat: eaten.

questions.prompt: drink → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of drink: drunk.

questions.prompt: drink → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of drink: drinks.

questions.prompt: She ___ rice with dinner every day. (eat)
questions.explanation: She eats rice with dinner every day. (eat)

questions.prompt: Yesterday, I ___ some water after lunch. (drink)
questions.explanation: Yesterday, I drank some water after lunch. (drink)

questions.prompt: Which word means “to take money out of a bank account”?
questions.explanation: withdraw: to take money out of a bank account. I need to withdraw cash from the ATM.

questions.prompt: _____ your paycheck into your bank account on payday.
questions.explanation: deposit: to put money into a bank account. Deposit your check before the end of the business day.

questions.prompt: Rosa checks the fridge before grocery shopping. Put the words in order. Words: How / many / eggs / do / we / have
answers: How many eggs do we have
questions.explanation: Eggs are countable, so use 'how many' and the plural form.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has an error?
options: There is too much oil in the pan.
I have a lot of eggs at home.
She bought a few rice for dinner.
answers: She bought a few rice for dinner.
questions.explanation: Rice is uncountable. You cannot say 'a few rice.' Use 'a little rice' instead.

questions.prompt: see → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of see: seen.

questions.prompt: see → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of see: sees.

questions.prompt: find → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of find: finds.

questions.prompt: find → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of find: finding.

questions.prompt: Did you ___ the apartment yesterday? (see)
questions.explanation: Did you see the apartment yesterday? (see)

questions.prompt: Where did you ___ the rental listing? (find)
questions.explanation: Where did you find the rental listing? (find)

questions.prompt: Do I _____ for the low-income housing program?
questions.explanation: qualify: to meet the requirements needed for something. Do I qualify for the low-income housing program?

questions.prompt: Which word means “to formally request something (a job, an apartment, a program)”?
questions.explanation: apply: to formally request something (a job, an apartment, a program). You need to apply online for that apartment.

questions.prompt: Rosa wants to ask the landlord about the nearest bus stop. Which question is correct?
questions.explanation: Information questions need inversion: question word + verb + subject. 'Where is the bus stop?' is correct.

questions.prompt: Rosa wants to ask about the price of rent. Which question word does she use?
questions.explanation: 'How much' asks about price or an uncountable amount. 'How many' is for countable things like bedrooms.

questions.prompt: choose → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of choose: chooses.

questions.prompt: choose → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of choose: choosing.

questions.prompt: let → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of let: letting.

questions.prompt: let → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of let: let.

questions.prompt: We have to ___ an apartment this week. (choose)
questions.explanation: We have to choose an apartment this week. (choose)

questions.prompt: The landlord doesn’t ___ tenants smoke inside. (let)
questions.explanation: The landlord doesn’t let tenants smoke inside. (let)

questions.prompt: Which word means “to look at two or more things to find differences”?
questions.explanation: compare: to look at two or more things to find differences. Compare the rent and size of each apartment.

questions.prompt: I can't _____ an apartment in that expensive neighborhood.
questions.explanation: afford: to have enough money to pay for something. I can't afford an apartment in that area.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "You ___ repaint the walls. That's the landlord's job." (Three words: not required.)
questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' means it is not your responsibility. 'Can't' would mean it is forbidden, which is different.

questions.prompt: The lease explains what the landlord must do before entering. Put the words in order. Words: The / landlord / has / to / give / notice
answers: The landlord has to give notice
questions.explanation: 'Has to' shows the landlord is legally required to give notice before entering.

verb-quiz-14.title: Weekly Quiz 14: Landlord Calls + Repair Requests

questions.prompt: break → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of break: breaking.

questions.prompt: break → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of break: broke.

questions.prompt: hold → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of hold: held.

questions.prompt: hold → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of hold: held.

questions.prompt: I need to report that the window ___ yesterday. (break)
questions.explanation: I need to report that the window broke yesterday. (break)

questions.prompt: Could you ___ the door open, please? (hold)
questions.explanation: Could you hold the door open, please? (hold)

questions.prompt: The landlord will _____ the apartment on Monday.
questions.explanation: inspect: to look at something carefully to check its condition. The landlord will inspect the apartment next Monday.

questions.prompt: Which word means “to fix something that is broken or damaged”?
questions.explanation: repair: to fix something that is broken or damaged. The landlord must repair the broken window within 24 hours.

questions.prompt: Carlos calls about an apartment on Bremen Street. Put the words in order. Words: I / would / like / to / meet / the / landlord
answers: I would like to meet the landlord
questions.explanation: 'Would like to' + base verb is the polite form. Use it for calls with landlords and offices.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: I want finding an apartment near the bus.
I want to finding an apartment near the bus.
I want to find an apartment near the bus.
answers: I want to find an apartment near the bus.
questions.explanation: After 'want', use 'to' + base verb. 'Finding' (-ing form) is not correct here.

questions.prompt: hear → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of hear: heard.

questions.prompt: hear → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of hear: heard.

questions.prompt: leave → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of leave: left.

questions.prompt: leave → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of leave: leaves.

questions.prompt: I was cooking when I ___ a loud noise. (hear)
questions.explanation: I was cooking when I heard a loud noise. (hear)

questions.prompt: While I was locking the door, my neighbor ___ the building. (leave)
questions.explanation: While I was locking the door, my neighbor left the building. (leave)

questions.prompt: Which word means “to stop something bad from happening”?
questions.explanation: prevent: to stop something bad from happening. Regular cleaning can prevent mold in the bathroom.

questions.prompt: The landlord agreed to _____ us for the plumber's bill.
questions.explanation: reimburse: to pay someone back for money they spent. The landlord agreed to reimburse us for the plumber's cost.

questions.prompt: Lucia was mopping the floor when the pipe burst. Which action was already in progress?
questions.explanation: Past continuous (was mopping) shows the background action in progress. Past simple (burst) is the event that interrupted it.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "While Lucia ___ the landlord, the kids woke up." (Action in progress: past continuous.)
questions.explanation: 'While' introduces the action that was in progress, so past continuous (was calling) is needed. 'Called' would use past simple.

questions.prompt: become → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of become: become.

questions.prompt: become → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of become: becomes.

questions.prompt: lead → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of lead: leads.

questions.prompt: lead → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of lead: leading.

questions.prompt: go → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of go: going.

questions.prompt: Before I applied, I had ___ a team leader. (become)
questions.explanation: Before I applied, I had become a team leader. (become)

questions.prompt: She had ___ two projects before her promotion. (lead)
questions.explanation: She had led two projects before her promotion. (lead)

questions.prompt: Check the _____ to see which days you work next week.
questions.explanation: schedule: your plan for the day or week. My work schedule changes every week.

questions.prompt: Which word means “a short rest from work”?
questions.explanation: break: a short rest from work. We take a 15-minute break at 10:00 AM.

questions.prompt: When the manager arrived, I had already finished my tasks. What happened first?
options: Both happened at exactly the same time.
questions.explanation: Had finished marks the earlier past action.

questions.prompt: Gloria finished her tasks before the manager arrived. Put the words in order. Words: She / had / finished / before / the / manager / arrived
answers: She had finished before the manager arrived
questions.explanation: Past Perfect (had finished) = the earlier action. Past Simple (arrived) = the later action.

verb-quiz-17.title: Weekly Quiz 17: Workplace Rules + Must, Have To, Should

questions.prompt: wear → V1-s (he/she/it)
questions.explanation: V1-s (he/she/it) of wear: wears.

questions.prompt: wear → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of wear: wearing.

questions.prompt: keep → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of keep: keeping.

questions.prompt: keep → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of keep: kept.

questions.prompt: leave → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of leave: left.

questions.prompt: You must ___ safety shoes here. (wear)
questions.explanation: You must wear safety shoes here. (wear)

questions.prompt: Employees have to ___ the exit clear. (keep)
questions.explanation: Employees have to keep the exit clear. (keep)

questions.prompt: Which word means “used to show permission or ability”?
questions.explanation: can: used to show permission or ability. You can take your break after you finish this task.

questions.prompt: Safety goggles are _____ when using the machines.
questions.explanation: required: necessary; must be done. A photo ID is required to enter the building.

questions.prompt: Claudette tells Linh: 'You ___ tell your supervisor before you leave the floor.' It's not a written rule, but it's important. Which word fits?
questions.explanation: When something is strong advice from experience but not a written rule, 'should' is the right modal.

questions.prompt: Which sentence has a grammar error?
options: He must wear a hard hat on the site.
She has to clocks in before her shift.
You should ask before swapping shifts.
answers: She has to clocks in before her shift.
questions.explanation: After 'has to,' use the base verb with no -s. The correct form is 'has to clock in,' not 'has to clocks in.'

questions.prompt: win → V-ing
questions.explanation: V-ing of win: winning.

questions.prompt: win → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of win: won.

questions.prompt: fly → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of fly: flew.

questions.prompt: fly → V3 (past participle)
questions.explanation: V3 (past participle) of fly: flown.

questions.prompt: If I ___ a free trip, I would visit my family. (win)
questions.explanation: If I won a free trip, I would visit my family. (win)

questions.prompt: If she ___ to Boston, I would meet her at the airport. (fly)
questions.explanation: If she flew to Boston, I would meet her at the airport. (fly)

questions.prompt: Eating at your desk is _____ if you clean up after.
questions.explanation: allowed: permitted; okay to do. Cell phones are not allowed during the test.

questions.prompt: Which word means “protection from danger or harm”?
questions.explanation: safety: protection from danger or harm. Safety is very important in the kitchen.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: "If I ___ you, I would call the agency." (Giving advice: use 'were' for all subjects.)
questions.explanation: In 'If I were you,' use 'were' for all subjects in the second conditional if-clause, not 'was' or 'am'.

questions.prompt: Kevin is likely to get overtime next week. Which sentence fits?
options: If they offered me overtime, I would say yes.
If they offer me overtime, I will say yes.
If they offered me overtime, I will say yes.
answers: If they offer me overtime, I will say yes.
questions.explanation: A real, likely future situation uses the first conditional: 'if + present simple, will + base verb'.

verb-quiz-19.title: Weekly Quiz 19: Phrasal Verbs at Work + Workplace Rights

questions.prompt: get → V2 (past)
questions.explanation: V2 (past) of get: got.
